title: Sci-Fi Evidence Scanner with Post-Processing Modes
description: A mysterious shoe has been found aboard a derelict spaceship hallway. The user operates a forensic evidence scanner that cycles through different post-processing vision modes to analyze the shoe artifact. Each mode reveals different visual information through bloom, pixelation, color grading, and edge detection effects.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with EffectComposer post-processing. Load space_ship_hallway.glb as the environment and place MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb on the hallway floor slightly off-center as a discovered artifact. Set the camera inside the hallway looking down at the shoe from a slight angle (first-person forensic investigator perspective). Add dim ambient light (0x334466) and a bright point light (0xaaccff) near the shoe simulating a scanner beam, plus subtle red emergency lights along the hallway walls. Set up EffectComposer with RenderPass as the base. Implement exactly 4 scanner vision modes the user cycles through: (1) NORMAL mode with UnrealBloomPass (strength 0.3, radius 0.4, threshold 0.85) for baseline sci-fi atmosphere, (2) THERMAL mode using ShaderPass with a custom shader that converts the image to a heat-map color ramp (blue to red) based on luminance, (3) SCAN-LINE mode using ShaderPass that adds horizontal green scan lines (every 3 pixels) plus FilmPass with scanline intensity 0.8 and grayscale enabled, (4) EVIDENCE mode combining UnrealBloomPass at high strength (1.5) with a vignette ShaderPass that darkens edges heavily to spotlight the shoe. Display the current mode name in a HUD overlay at the top-left (styled as a sci-fi terminal readout with monospace green text). Clicking anywhere on the canvas cycles to the next mode with the HUD updating. Add a checkbox labeled 'Rotate Artifact' that toggles slow Y-axis rotation on the shoe model. Add a range slider labeled 'Scanner Intensity' (0.0 to 2.0) that multiplies the bloom strength in modes 1 and 4 and the scanline opacity in mode 3. Ensure all post-processing passes are properly enabled/disabled when switching modes. Use OrbitControls with limited vertical range so the user can look around the hallway but stays roughly at standing height.
